orphan_groups: O1 — the attribution ladder (evidence that a set of addresses is one entity)
O2 — the public-record timeline (announcements/assurances with utterance timestamps)
O3 — the gap ledger (paired on-chain event t0, statement t1, delta)
O4 — query provenance (explorer, dataset vintage, block height) — content, no finding opened

scored_criteria.criterion: address / cluster / entity are three distinct fact classes and never merge

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project — the chain record vs the public explanation
findings.title: facts[] cannot carry a measured component and an inferred attribution about the same object
findings.expected: A fact about one object (a transfer attributed to a cluster) should be able to declare that its quantitative component is hash-verified while its attribution component is an inference — two evidence classes, one fact.
findings.got: facts[] is {id, claim, load_bearing, source, confidence, as_of, note?} with a single scalar confidence whose documented semantics are SOURCE RELIABILITY ('Vendor research is low by default'). Setting it high launders the attribution to the certainty of a blockchain; setting it medium demotes a block-verified transfer to analyst-grade. confidenceNote is optional free text and appears nowhere in the schema's 'Consumed by' table, so nothing downstream reads it.
findings.content_or_lens_argument: Marked content per the rubric default, but it is honestly NEITHER: no rewording of the domain table or the column labels adds a field to facts[]. It is a shared-mechanism gap whose fix (an evidence_class enum on facts[]) helps every Creator with a two-class object — OSINT geolocation vs unit attribution, breach artifact vs actor attribution, die-shot vs yield. That is the opposite of a lens.
findings.refuter_pass: Refuted? No. (a) 'Is this the topic being genuinely hard?' — the two-class object is the ordinary shape of forensic evidence, not an exotic case. (b) 'Would a competent execution have produced this anyway?' — a careful researcher writes it into note[], which env.md:34-35 explicitly names as a workaround, not a fix. (c) 'Present somewhere unread?' — grepped the repo; the only evidence-class vocabulary is knowledge/README.md:36-41, scoped by its own text to PATTERNS.md claims about the video corpus. Holds.
findings.l2_priority: Attempt a real fact for one transfer attributed to a cluster, and record which confidence value the run picked and what it silently claimed.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: No fact-to-fact relation: splitting a two-class claim loses the binding, and loses it across a column boundary
findings.expected: If the measured transfer and the inferred attribution must be two facts, the notebook should record that one qualifies the other, so descoping the attribution wounds the transfer's phrasing.
findings.got: Every relation in the model points upward from facts to a synthesis — reversals[].evidence[], conclusions.restsOn, currency.expires_first/durable are all id lists. There is no about / subject / qualifies / depends_on edge between facts. After the split the binding survives only inside two one-line claim strings, and Rule 1 forbids prose. Worse, CARD_DIMENSION is one dimension per card, so the transfer files under flows and the attribution under actors: a reviewer descoping the attribution leaves a flows card still reading 'Cluster C moved…', and the wound graph has no edge to propagate along because it models conclusion->fact only.
findings.refuter_pass: Refuted? No. Tried 'the researcher can just write both halves into one claim string' — that is G-l1s-cc-01's failure, not an escape. Tried 'note[] carries it' — note is not consumed by any composition step (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:14-22). The column-boundary consequence is the part that survives every refutation, because it makes the loss happen after human review rather than before it.
findings.l2_priority: Write both facts, then simulate descoping the attribution card and check whether the surviving card still asserts the entity.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: The MEASURED / OBSERVED / INFERRED / ASSUMED ladder is not in the notebook contract at all
findings.expected: Per gauntlet/rubric.md:62 and SKILL.md:90, a notebook fact carries a rung on the evidence ladder.
findings.got: No notebook artifact references the ladder. It exists only at knowledge/README.md:36-41, and its own text scopes it to PATTERNS.md — 'Every line in a PATTERNS.md carries one' — i.e. it governs the studio's claims about its VIDEO CORPUS, not a notebook's claims about the world. The notebook's honesty vocabulary is `confidence: high|medium|low`, which is a source-reliability axis, not an evidence-class axis. CONTRADICTS the brief's second hypothesis in an unexpected direction: there is no rung for interpretive evidence because there is no ladder.
findings.refuter_pass: Refuted to 'present-but-missed'? Considered and rejected. The ladder IS present in the repo, but scoped by its own sentence to a different artifact class; applying it to notebook facts would be an extension, not a discovery. Recording confirmed-absent for the notebook contract and naming the near-miss explicitly so the judge can rule it a scope decision if it prefers.
findings.l2_priority: Confirm whether a live run spontaneously reaches for MEASURED/INFERRED language in `note` because `confidence` cannot express it.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: scale_conversions[].felt is an unconstrained promotion path from address-cohort to named people — demonstrated in the reference run
findings.expected: The conversion that makes a number felt should not be permitted to change the CLASS of the subject (addresses -> cohort -> people) without a flag.
findings.got: scale_conversions is {raw, felt} with one documented constraint ('a number without a comparison is a number the script wastes') and no honesty constraint. In the incumbent run: f-lth-distribution is correctly written as an address-cohort measurement; scale_conversions.felt renders it as 'the PEOPLE who held longest sold most'; conclusion c-borrowed-prosperity renders it as 'people who believed in it'; script--adjudication.md says it aloud. Three hops, no flag, entirely inside the sanctioned pipeline. Harmless on Bitcoin, where nobody is accused; on a collapsed project hop two is a defamation exposure sourced to a raw/felt pair.
findings.refuter_pass: Refuted? No. 'Is this my topic being hard?' — the demonstration is in the incumbent's own artifact on the incumbent's own topic, so it is the mechanism, not my domain. 'Would competent execution avoid it?' — a competent execution DID this; Phase 5 (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:78-86) actively rewards the vivid conversion and never mentions subject class.
findings.l2_priority: Check every scale_conversion in a produced fraud notebook for a subject-class change between raw and felt.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: No naming policy on conclusions, and a compound claim discharges falsifiableBy by falsifying only its checkable half
findings.expected: A conclusion asserting that a named individual controls a wallet cluster should be gated on a filing or an admission, and its falsifier should bind the load-bearing (naming) half of the claim.
findings.got: conclusions.ts has no namesPerson flag, no evidence-class requirement on a naming conclusion, and no gate at all. The `unhinged` tier is self-defined as 'a claim about MOTIVE, which is the least verifiable kind of claim there is', and the shipped exemplar c-reserve-was-the-product imputes motive to a named sitting head of state ('a way to put a floor under an asset your donors hold'), then discharges falsifiableBy with 'a funded, audited reserve with a published coin count' — which falsifies only the near, checkable half. Publish the audited reserve and the donor-motive imputation is untouched. The `hottest` 'HIGHER bar' turns out to be 'it still states a falsifier', satisfied decoratively.
findings.content_or_lens_argument: The only finding here I would argue is genuinely lens. 'exposure-class' and 'conclusion-policy: max leap, falsifier standard, NAMING RULES' are literally named lens fields in SKILL.md:193-198, and no rewording of a domain table adds a gate. The judge may reasonably reply that a compound-claim rule (the falsifier must bind the load-bearing half) is a universal repair to the shared mechanism — I would accept that, and it would still not supply the filing-or-admission gate.
findings.refuter_pass: This CONFIRMS an orchestrator lead, which the brief warns is the failure mode of a primed walker. Stated deliberately: the lead proposed that the falsifier requirement MIGHT already constrain unhinged adequately. I found a specific mechanism by which it does not — compound claim, partial falsifier — derived from the shipped exemplar rather than from the lead. Refuter 'is this by-design?' checked against accepted-gaps.md:36-45, which accepts that conclusions have no SOURCES because the falsifier substitutes; that acceptance explicitly names an uncheckable falsifier as a real finding, and a falsifier bound to the wrong half is the same defect wearing a checkable coat.
findings.l2_priority: Generate a conclusion naming a person for this topic and test whether the produced falsifier binds the naming clause or a neighbouring checkable one.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: mechanisms[] has no evidence[] field — the causal spine is the only unsourced structure in the notebook
findings.expected: The structure that authors the beat chain, and that the script step inherits wholesale, should carry evidence per link.
findings.got: mechanisms[] is {id, name, chain[], explains, needs_analogy, note?} — no evidence[], while reversals[] one section down has one. Phase 3 never asks for per-link evidence, and the quality bar checks only that every chain link is BUT or THEREFORE — a form check, not a support check. This is where my event->statement gap has to live once it cannot be a fact (see G-l1s-cc-07), so my load-bearing measurement ends up in an unsourced, undated, unconfidenced prose string.
findings.refuter_pass: Partially refuted, and downgraded because of it. A mechanism can inherit evidence transitively via a reversal that names it (r1 carries evidence[] and mechanism: m-etf-plumbing). Real, so this is major not blocker. But m-institutionalisation's chain has five links against r4's three fact ids with no per-link binding, and a mechanism no reversal points at inherits nothing. Confirmed at reduced severity.
findings.l2_priority: Count chain links with no traceable supporting fact in a produced notebook.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: as_of is a currency field, not an event-time field, so the gap between an on-chain event and a public statement cannot be a sourced fact
findings.expected: The delta between when something happened on-chain and when it was said in public is the thesis of the topic; it should be a first-class dated, sourced fact.
findings.got: as_of is documented as driving `currency` — a staleness axis — is date-only with no time component, and there is one of it per fact. It cannot distinguish event time from discovery time from utterance time. Writing the gap as its own fact ('the outflow preceded the assurance by 19 days') produces a claim with two sources, two dates and two confidences, which cannot honestly satisfy the quality bar's 'every fact has a source, a date and a confidence' — and, per G-l1s-cc-02, has no edge to the two facts it is computed from. The remaining home is a mechanism chain string, which carries no evidence at all (G-l1s-cc-06). Named orphan groups O2 and O3.
findings.refuter_pass: Refuted? No. Tried 'derived facts are fine, just cite both sources in the source string' — the source field is a single string and the incumbent already abuses it that way (notebook.json:26, '99bitcoins / investingnews price history'), which is precisely the laundering the schema's own anti-patterns section warns about. Tried 'this is a timeline feature, not a schema gap' — a timeline is a rendering; the claim 'nineteen days' is an assertion that needs a confidence.
findings.l2_priority: Attempt to write three gap facts and record which quality-bar checkbox each one fails.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: The actors column's emptyMeans instructs the researcher to name people, and one column holds three ontological tiers
findings.expected: In a domain where address, cluster and entity are three distinct classes, the board should keep them distinct — and an empty actors column should not read as a reprimand.
findings.got: One `actors` column with emptyMeans 'Nobody is named — the story has no agents'. env.md:12-13 says an emptyMeans is a claim about what an empty column signifies and must be tested; this one is false in a forensic domain, where a story can have agents that are clusters and where declining to name is the professional standard rather than a research failure. The result is that the attribution ladder (orphan O1) lands in `actors` and becomes indistinguishable from the attribution itself.
findings.refuter_pass: Refuted? No, but scoped down. The emptyMeans string is cheap to fix and is unambiguously content. The 'one column, three tiers' half is closer to structural, but a lens that splits actors into address/cluster/entity columns is not justified while G-l1s-cc-01 remains unfixed — with an evidence_class on facts, one actors column would hold all three honestly. Recording as content on that basis.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether a produced fraud notebook's actors column mixes address-tier and entity-tier cards.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: No D-rigged tell for a steel-man sourced entirely to the accused
findings.expected: The D-honest checklist should catch the fraud-domain default failure: a counter-case that is present, prominent and at full strength, but whose only source is the subject of the accusation.
findings.got: ENGINES.md gives three structural tells, all concerned with whether counter-evidence was PRE-EXCLUDED. None addresses the inverse — a counter-case that is included but is the defendant's own statement, which in fraud is the most available, most articulate and cheapest steel-man there is. That is a right-of-reply box wearing the steel-man's coat, and the checklist would score it a clean pass. Related: Engine D's verdict step, in this domain, is a finding of culpability, and nothing in the catalogue asks whether a verdict is PERMITTED as opposed to well-weighed.
findings.refuter_pass: Refuted? No, but note the honest tension: the incumbent's own steel-man (f-mstr-defence) IS partly the subject's statement — 'Saylor claims it can cover $6bn of debt' — and there it is entirely appropriate, because the subject is not accused of anything. That is exactly why the tell is missing: the reference topic could not have surfaced it. A fourth tell ('name a counter-case source with no stake in the verdict') is content, not a lens.
findings.l2_priority: Audit the produced steel-man's sources for independence from the subject.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: No engine whose pleasure is verification; Engine B fuses 'operable mechanism' with 'trivially small payoff'
findings.expected: A catalogue of viewer pleasures should contain the one forensic audiences come for — watching a claim get checked against a record — and should not disqualify an engine by an outcome the material happens not to have.
findings.got: Seven engines, none of whose pleasure is verification. D's is 'watching a question get settled' by an author, which is adjacent but is adjudication, not checking. Separately, Engine B's shape hard-codes 'trivially small payoff' into a structure whose genuinely transferable part is 'a mechanism a viewer could operate' — a wallet trace is the latter and emphatically not the former, so the engine that best fits the procedure is ruled out by an unrelated clause. Also noted: the chooser table would never have surfaced Engine F for a trace, though hop depth is textbook naturally-ordered difficulty.
findings.refuter_pass: Substantially weakened on refutation and marked uncertain because of it. ENGINES.md:13 declares the catalogue 'open, not settled' and :172-175 says engines compose — a verification engine may simply be A composed with D, and the honest answer at L1 is that I cannot tell without writing the script. Recording uncertain rather than inflating a taxonomy preference into a gap.
findings.l2_priority: Render this notebook through A and through D and report whether either delivers a verification pleasure or only an assertion one.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: One dimension per card: the sector drawdown series is simultaneously macro evidence and counter-case evidence
findings.expected: A card that is load-bearing in two columns should be visible in both, or descoping it in one should warn about the other.
findings.got: CARD_DIMENSION is Record<string, DimensionId> — exactly one dimension per card. My strongest counter-case support ('this was market conditions') is the same series as my macro context, so descoping it from macro silently removes the counter-case's best evidence from a column whose own emptyMeans is marked DANGEROUS.
findings.refuter_pass: Largely refuted, kept at minor/uncertain for the record. A researcher can legitimately write two cards from two angles — the macro claim and the counter-argument built on it are arguably different claims. Recording honestly rather than pretending it is structural.
findings.l2_priority: Note any card the run wanted in two columns.

findings.creator: crypto-collapse
findings.topic: on-chain post-mortem of a collapsed project
findings.title: Phase 1's domain table is declared market-only with no substitution rule, and there is no primary-data step
findings.expected: A non-market topic should be told how to derive its own Phase 1 domain rows, and a topic whose evidence is primary data should be told to go and get it.
findings.got: Phase 1 says 'For a market/economics topic, that is at minimum:' and then gives six rows, with no instruction for any other topic shape. A forensic run improvises its own domains, which is exactly where an evidence floor gets set silently. Phase 1 is also a web-search protocol end to end — the reference run's own research_gaps confesses 'Still no PRIMARY on-chain data… every figure remains aggregator-sourced' and rendered three scripts anyway. My baseline is 13h of which ~10h is clustering from primary data, and no phase of the methodic touches it: ~110 min saved against a 120 min acceptance bar, and negative if the notebook's cluster assertions are trusted.
findings.refuter_pass: Refuted in part. 'Is the substitution rule present somewhere unread?' — Phase 8 and the notebook's subject_domain field imply topic variation exists, but neither instructs Phase 1; confirmed-absent stands. 'Is the missing primary-data step by design?' — plausibly yes at prototype scope (accepted-gaps.md:23-32 accepts that the app cannot run research at all), which is why this is minor rather than major despite driving the time-saved fail. The domain-table half is unambiguously content: add forensic rows.
findings.l2_priority: Record the actual search count and whether any primary chain data was reached; if zero, the time-saved estimate is confirmed optimistic.
